summary: @ornikar/apollo-link-timeout preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes hidden obfuscated payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that downloads the Bun runtime from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<arch>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a bundled file `math_init.js` at the package root. If a `bun` binary is already present on the system it is used to execute `math_init.js` directly. `math_init.js` is a ~700KB obfuscated bundle (hex identifier names, rotated string-array indirection, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) that is not listed in `package.json`'s `files` field (which declares only `lib`) yet ships in the tarball, and is unrelated to the advertised Apollo link timeout functionality implemented in `lib/timeoutLink.js`. The `setup.mjs` loader itself is likewise obfuscated. The package name is a scoped lookalike of the legitimate `apollo-link-timeout`. Using a second language runtime to execute a hidden payload evades Node-based static and dynamic analysis; combined with the obfuscation, undeclared blob, and package-name resemblance, this is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape and fires automatically on `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
